one_line: A master sculptor of early medieval Kamarupa, shaping the famed Da Parbatiya stone doorway near Tezpur.

appearance.age_look: Late 20s to early 30s, lean but strong artisan’s build with defined arms and shoulders from stone work.
appearance.face: Oval face with high cheekbones, medium-brown Assamese complexion, straight nose, slightly thick lips, soft calloused hands, a faint stone-dust scar on the left cheek; default expression is focused and quietly proud, as if visualising intricate carvings.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair drawn back into a low knot at the back of the head, with a few loose strands at the temples; a simple off-white cloth headband tied around the forehead to keep dust and sweat away, knotted at the back with short tails.
appearance.costume: A knee-length cotton angarkha-style upper garment in muted terracotta red, crossing left over right and tied with inner and outer cloth strings; sleeves are three-quarter length, close but not tight, with a narrow off-white border at the cuffs; wrapped below the waist is a handwoven off-white cotton dhoti-like lower garment with a subtle faint-grey check pattern, pleated in front and reaching just above the ankles; a narrow woven waist sash in deep indigo is tied firmly over the angarkha, with its ends tucked into the left side; around his neck, a simple dark wooden bead mala; on his feet, plain brown leather sandals with a toe loop; his forearms bear thin coiled brass bangles for a touch of subtle ornament, and a small square of cloth is tucked at the sash for wiping stone dust.
appearance.signature: A mid-length iron-tipped stone-carver’s chisel with a slightly flared cutting edge and a polished wooden mallet with a rounded head, both carried together—chisel held in his right hand and mallet in his left—often shown with faint stone dust on them.

ref_desc: A lean medium-brown Assamese artisan in a terracotta-red angarkha, off-white checked dhoti, deep-indigo waist sash, black hair in a low knot with off-white headband, wooden mala, brass bangles, brown sandals, carrying a dusty stone-carver’s chisel and wooden mallet.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of a lean medium-brown Assamese male artisan from early medieval Kamarupa, late 20s, with an oval face, high cheekbones, focused proud expression, and thick black hair pulled into a low knot at the back with a simple off-white cloth headband tied around his forehead; give him a knee-length terracotta-red cotton angarkha crossing left over right, three-quarter sleeves with narrow off-white borders, and a handwoven off-white cotton dhoti-like lower garment with a faint grey check pattern, pleated in front and falling to just above the ankles; tie a deep-indigo woven sash firmly around his waist over the angarkha, tucking a small wiping cloth at the left side, and add a simple dark wooden bead mala around his neck, thin brass bangles on his forearms, and plain brown leather sandals with a toe loop; place a mid-length iron-tipped stone-carver’s chisel with a slightly flared edge in his right hand and a rounded wooden mallet in his left, both lightly dusted with stone powder; use a palette of terracotta red, off-white, deep indigo, brown, and brass gold, and show him from multiple angles to emphasise the consistent face, low-knot hairstyle with headband, detailed garments, sash, jewellery, and signature tools.
